Bedrock Text:  # How a Rainbow Forms  A rainbow forms when sunlight passes through water droplets in the air, usually after rain. The sunlight bends as it enters each droplet, separates into different colors, bounces off the back of the droplet, and bends again as it exits. This bending process, called refraction, separates white sunlight into the spectrum of colors we see—red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. You see a rainbow when the sun is behind you and water droplets are in front of you at the right angle.

Bedrock Text:  # Virus vs. Bacteria  **Bacteria** are single-celled living organisms with their own DNA and the ability to reproduce independently. They can survive on their own and some are actually beneficial to us.  **Viruses** are much smaller and aren’t technically alive—they’re genetic material (DNA or RNA) wrapped in protein. They can only reproduce by invading cells and hijacking their machinery.  In practical terms. bacteria can often be treated with antibiotics, while viruses cannot, and viruses typically cause more acute illnesses that your immune system must fight off.
